body:
### Problem

On 0.13-dev, writing a normal file buffer (buftype == "", non-empty name, modifiable, not readonly) intermittently writes to a different filename than the buffer's own. The filename that gets used is the contents of an unrelated internal string. Observed cases:

``` Written filename | What that string actually is -- | -- 0{,0},0),0],:,0#,!^F,o,O,e | the default value of 'cinkeys' v:lua.vim.treesitter.foldexpr() | the value of 'foldexpr' autopairs map key | a desc field from an nvim-autopairs keymap ```

So: at least one chunk has to go through the message pipeline. A redraw is not sufficient, and forcing a fresh read of the buffer name is not sufficient. Plain Lua print() also works, so the effect is not specific to nvim_echo; what matters is that a message is actually emitted.

Steps to reproduce

I do not yet have a --clean reproduction — it needs my plugin set and is timing-dependent. What triggers it for me:

  1. Open a file via a Telescope picker.
  2. Edit somewhere other than line 1 (the buffer must be 'modified', or :update/:x no-ops and nothing happens).
  3. Trigger the write from a Lua keymap callback — not by typing :w or :update at the command line, which never reproduces it. Mine is an escalating <Esc> plugin, so the write happens inside a vim.keymap.set(..., function() ... end) callback.

Frequency is maybe 1 in 10–20 writes. It does not reproduce on a buffer opened directly with :e, only after picker-driven buffer switching — though that may just be a timing correlation rather than Telescope's involvement.

Relevant plugins loaded: telescope.nvim, nvim-autopairs, and a small rooter plugin that calls vim.cmd.lcd() from a BufEnter autocmd (so cwd changes frequently). Happy to bisect the plugin set if that would help.

Expected behavior

:write writes to the buffer's own filename.

Nvim version

NVIM v0.13.0-nightly+b997265
Build type: Release
LuaJIT 2.1.1774638290

Nix-packaged build (neovim-unwrapped-b997265).

Nvim only? / Last known working

0.12.4 is unaffected with the identical config. Only 0.13-dev is affected. I have not bisected the nightlies.

Operating system / terminal

macOS (APFS) — <paste your terminal emulator here>

Possibly related

ui2/messages.lua throws while rendering a deprecation warning — see Issue 2 below. Both are in the message subsystem, which is new this cycle, so they may share a cause.

### Steps to reproduce i'm not sure ### Expected behavior I expect it to save normally and not create garbage files ### Nvim version (nvim -v) NVIM v0.13.0-nightly+b997265 ### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same? i'm not sure ### Operating system/version macOS Tahoe ### Terminal name/version ghostty ### $TERM environment variable xterm-256color ### Installation Nix nightly overlay

This is not necessarily a "regression". ~~And the issue title ":write targets garbage filename" is 100% misleading: that is a random effect of this `feedkeys()` thing you are doing.~~ (Edit: I was wrong!)

If you are using `nvim_feedkeys(":saveas",..)` to perform programmatic actions, more keys (from other sources, e.g. plugins) may enter typahead at *any random time*. And `feedkeys()` has a bunch of flags to control that; but it should still be a last resort. There is likely a much more reliable approach (I didn't read most of the comments above, too much noise; need a minimal repro).

Feeding `<cmd>` instead of `:` will help, but it looks like you're intentionally leaving the ":" cmdline prompt open so that you can feed the filename into it later. That can easily get "regressed" if some other asynchrnous task feeds keys in the middle (which is not a regression, just a consequence of using `feedkeys()`).

OTOH, it is also possible that ui2 is doing something yucky. So if you can provide a minimal repro, we can dig into that.

**To reproduce:**

2. Move off line 1, enter insert, type something, leave insert
3. Hit F5 then F6 as fast as you can 

F5 does window teardown (closes floats, nohlsearch). F6 just calls vim.cmd("w").

Hit them fast enough and the write goes to the wrong filename. Not a mangled version of the real name — a completely unrelated internal string.

When I press the two keys slowly, everything works as expected.  So I have to conclude it's a race.   

If I disable ui2... I can press those keys as quickly as I can and I get no incorrect filenames, so the race only seems to be happening in ui2.

* If I restore all my plugins and make them active (where it calls things like treesitter) that's when I'll start getting those weird longer filenames and the E212 "illegal byte sequence" -- likely from more complex names like `v:lua.vim.treesitter.foldexpr()` and `0{,0},0),0],:,0#,!^F,o,O,e`

* Adding any message before the write (print("x") or nvim_echo) makes it stop completely. Perhaps it simply allows the race to finish?
* Typing :w by hand has never once done it — only writes from a Lua callback, which makes sense because I can't type fast enough to catch the race condition
